claim: 797 natural Arabidopsis thaliana accessions were measured for glucosinolate variation in seeds
source: Here, we measure the variation in specialized metabolites across a population of 797 natural Arabidopsis thaliana accessions.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the number of accessions measured in the study population.

claim: A combination of geography, environmental parameters, demography and different genetic processes all combine to influence the specific chemotypes and their distribution
source: We show that a combination of geography, environmental parameters, demography and different genetic processes all combine to influence the specific chemotypes and their distribution.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract based on the study's analyses.

claim: Causal loci in specialized metabolism contain frequent independently generated alleles with patterns suggesting potential within-species convergence
source: This showed that causal loci in specialized metabolism contain frequent independently generated alleles with patterns suggesting potential within-species convergence.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract based on genetic analyses.

claim: Plants produce diverse metabolites to cope with the challenges presented by complex and ever-changing environments
source: Plants produce diverse metabolites to cope with the challenges presented by complex and ever-changing environments.
evidence: This is a general statement supported by established scientific knowledge and citations in the introduction.

claim: Individual specialized metabolites can defend the plant against some stressors while simultaneously making the plant more sensitive to other biotic or abiotic stresses
source: For example, individual specialized metabolites can defend the plant against some stressors while simultaneously making the plant more sensitive to other biotic or abiotic stresses (Agrawal, 2000; Bialy et al., 1990; Erb and Kliebenstein, 2020; Futuyma and Agrawal, 2009; Hu et al., 2018; Lankau, 2007; Opitz and Müller, 2009; Uremıs et al., 2009; Züst and Agrawal, 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: Metabolic variation within and between species is the result of structural variation at the enzymes responsible for the chemical structures, or variation at the expression levels of these enzymes
source: A common finding of these studies is that the metabolic variation within and between species is the result of structural variation at the enzymes responsible for the chemical structures, or variation at the expression levels of these enzymes, which contributes to the quantitative variation in specialized metabolism (Chan et al., 2011; Chan et al., 2010; Fan et al., 2019; Kroymann et al., 2003; Moore et al., 2019; Schilmiller et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: Structural and regulatory variants and the resulting chemical variation strongly influence plant fitness in response to a broad range of biotic interactions including herbivores and other plant species
source: These structural and regulatory variants and the resulting chemical variation strongly influence plant fitness in response to a broad range of biotic interactions including herbivores and other plant species (Bednarek and Osbourn, 2009; Brachi et al., 2015; Kerwin et al., 2017; Kerwin et al., 2015; Lankau and Kliebenstein, 2009; Lankau and Strauss, 2007; Lankau, 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: The potential for genetic variants influencing plant chemical variation is derived from the enhanced proportion of gene duplication in enzyme encoding genes for specialized metabolism
source: The potential for these genetic variants influencing plant chemical variation is derived from the enhanced proportion of gene duplication in enzyme encoding genes for specialized metabolism, both at the local and whole genome level (Kliebenstein et al., 2001c; Moghe and Last, 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: 23 different glucosinolates were detected and quantified in the accession collection
source: 23 different GSLs were detected and quantified, identifying a wide diversity in composition and amount among the natural accessions with a median heritability of 83%, ranging from 34% to 93% (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is a direct measurement result from the study.

claim: The median heritability of glucosinolates is 83%, ranging from 34% to 93%
source: 23 different GSLs were detected and quantified, identifying a wide diversity in composition and amount among the natural accessions with a median heritability of 83%, ranging from 34% to 93% (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is a statistical result calculated from the study data.

claim: The first two principal components only captured 33% of the total variation in glucosinolate accumulation
source: The first two PCs only captured 33% of the total variation with PC1 describing GSLs with four and seven carbons and PC2 mainly capturing GSLs with eight carbons in their side chain (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a result from principal component analysis of the data.

claim: PC1 describes glucosinolates with four and seven carbons in their side chain
source: The first two PCs only captured 33% of the total variation with PC1 describing GSLs with four and seven carbons and PC2 mainly capturing GSLs with eight carbons in their side chain (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a result from principal component analysis of the data.

claim: PC2 mainly captures glucosinolates with eight carbons in their side chain
source: The first two PCs only captured 33% of the total variation with PC1 describing GSLs with four and seven carbons and PC2 mainly capturing GSLs with eight carbons in their side chain (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a result from principal component analysis of the data.

claim: Previous work suggested a simple continental gradient chain-elongation variation from the south-west to the north-east in central European accessions
source: Previous work using a collection of predominantly central European accessions had suggested a simple continental gradient chain-elongation variation from the south-west (SW) (that is enriched with alkenyl and hydroxyalkenyl GSLs) to the north-east (NE) (Brachi et al., 2015; Züst et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The larger collection shows that there is not a single gradient shaping glucosinolate diversity across Europe
source: This larger collection shows that there is not a single gradient shaping GSL diversity across Europe (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is a finding from the current study's analysis of geographic patterns.

claim: The SW to NE pattern reiterates within the Iberian Peninsula
source: Instead, the extended sampling of accessions around the Mediterranean Basin in this collection shows that the SW to NE pattern reiterates within the Iberian Peninsula.
evidence: This is a finding from the current study's analysis of geographic patterns.

claim: In both the Iberian Peninsula and Central Europe, the SW is enriched with C4 glucosinolates, and the NE with C3 glucosinolates
source: In each of these areas (Iberian Peninsula and Central Europe), the SW is enriched with C4 GSLs, and the NE with C3 GSLs (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the current study's analysis of geographic patterns.

claim: Genome-wide association analyses identified two major peaks covering two of the known causal gene clusters controlling glucosinolate diversity
source: In spite of the large population size, both PC1- and PC2-based analyses identified the same two major peaks covering two of the known causal gene clusters controlling GSL diversity (Figure 3B for PC1 GWA analyses, Figure 3—figure supplement 2B for PC2 GWA analyses) (Brachi et al., 2015; Chan et al., 2011; Chan et al., 2010).
evidence: This is a result from genome-wide association analysis.

claim: The largest peak in genome-wide association is the GS-Elong locus on chromosome 5, containing the MAM1, MAM2 and MAM3 genes
source: The largest peak in both cases is the GS-Elong locus on chromosome 5, containing the MAM1 (AT5G23010), MAM2 (that is not present in Col-0 plants) and MAM3 (AT5G23020) genes.
evidence: This is a result from genome-wide association analysis.

claim: The peak on chromosome 4 is the GS-AOP locus containing the AOP2 and AOP3 genes
source: The peak on chromosome 4 is the GS-AOP locus containing the AOP2 and AOP3 genes (AT4G03060 and AT4G03050, respectively).
evidence: This is a result from genome-wide association analysis.

claim: None of the other known natural variants within the glucosinolate biosynthetic pathway were identified by genome-wide association
source: Surprisingly, none of the other known natural variants within the GSL biosynthetic pathway (listed in Supplementary file 2) were identified by GWA including three that were found with 96 accessions and three that were found with 595 accessions using PC1 and 2 (Brachi et al., 2015; Chan et al., 2011; Chan et al., 2010; Kliebenstein, 2009).
evidence: This is a result from genome-wide association analysis compared to prior studies.

claim: Most accessions were classified as 2-OH-3-Butenyl (27%) or Allyl (47%) chemotypes
source: Most accessions were classified as 2-OH-3-Butenyl (27%) or Allyl (47%) with lower frequencies for the other chemotypes.
evidence: This is a result from chemotype classification of the accessions.

claim: Central and parts of Northern Europe were characterized by a high variability involving the co-occurrence of individuals from all chemotypes
source: Central and parts of Northern Europe (like north Germany and Poland) were characterized by a high variability involving the co-occurrence of individuals from all chemotypes.
evidence: This is a finding from the geographic analysis of chemotype distribution.

claim: Southern Europe has two predominant chemotypes, Allyl or 2-OH-3-Butenyl, that are separated from each other by a clear and sharp geographic partitioning
source: In contrast, southern Europe, which presents a dense sampling, including the Iberian Peninsula, Italy and the Balkan, has two predominant chemotypes, Allyl or 2-OH-3-Butenyl, that are separated from each other by a clear and sharp geographic partitioning (Figure 4 and Figure 4—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is a finding from the geographic analysis of chemotype distribution.

claim: Swedish accessions displayed a striking presence of almost solely Allyl chemotypes
source: Uniquely, Swedish accessions displayed a striking presence of almost solely Allyl chemotypes.
evidence: This is a finding from the geographic analysis of chemotype distribution.

claim: Environmental conditions have different relationships to the chemotypes that shift by geographic areas
source: The models showed that the environmental conditions have different relationships to the chemotypes that shift by geographic areas.
evidence: This is a result from linear modeling of environmental and chemotype data.

claim: Min temp of coldest month and precipitation of wettest month have a significant interaction with geography
source: Moreover, two of the parameters (min temp of coldest month and precipitation of wettest month) have a significant interaction with geography, suggesting that the relationship of these environmental parameters to specific GSL chemotypes is different between Northern and Southern Europe (Table 1; for details on the models, see Methods).
evidence: This is a result from linear modeling showing statistical interactions.

claim: The accessions were distributed across eight distinctive clades in the MAM3 phylogeny with each clade clustering accessions having either a C3 or C4 phenotype
source: The accessions were distributed across eight distinctive clades with each clade clustering accessions having either a C3 or C4 phenotype (Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1 for bootstrap support).
evidence: This is a result from phylogenetic analysis of MAM3 sequences.

claim: Three of the MAM3 clades express C3 (MAM2) and five clades express C4 (MAM1)
source: The clades C3/C4 status altered across the tree with three of the clades expressing C3 (MAM2) and five clades expressing the C4 (MAM1).
evidence: This is a result from phylogenetic analysis combined with chemotype data.

claim: Clade 6 accessions have a haplotype that contains a chimeric MAM gene that combines the 5′ of MAM2 with the 3′ of MAM1
source: This showed that clade 6 are accessions that have a haplotype that contains a previously described chimeric MAM gene that combines the 5′ of MAM2 with the 3′ of MAM1 (Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 2; Benderoth et al., 2006; Kroymann et al., 2003).
evidence: This is a result from long-read sequencing and structural analysis.

claim: In clade 6 accessions, the chimeric gene leads to predominantly C3 glucosinolates
source: In these accessions, the chimeric gene leads to predominantly C3 GSLs.
evidence: This is a result linking genotype to phenotype.

claim: Clade 7 has a haplotype that is highly similar to clade 2 with a single copy of MAM1 leading to C4 glucosinolates
source: Clade 7 has a haplotype that is highly similar to clade 2 with a single copy of MAM1 leading to C4 GSLs.
evidence: This is a result from long-read sequencing and structural analysis.

claim: There is extensive mixing of nearly all major European GS-Elong haplotypes in Iberia, except clade 3 that is not present
source: As expected given that genetic variation in Iberia results from a series of range expansions from Central Europe and Africa (Lee et al., 2017; Durvasula et al., 2017), there is extensive mixing of nearly all major European GS-Elong haplotypes in Iberia, except of clade 3 that is not present.
evidence: This is a finding from geographic analysis of haplotype distribution combined with prior demographic knowledge.

claim: There is a sharp partitioning between the C3/C4 chemotypes in Iberia
source: In contrast, there is a sharp partitioning between the C3/C4 chemotypes created by these haplotypes.
evidence: This is a finding from geographic analysis of chemotype distribution.

claim: The strong geographic partitioning of the C3/C4 chemotypes in Iberia may be driven by selective pressure enhancing the partitioning of the chemotypes, and not solely neutral demographic processes
source: The strong geographic separation between the two chemotypes involving nearly all causal haplotypes (Figure 5—figure supplement 4) raises the possibility that the strong geographic partitioning of the C3/C4 chemotypes in Iberia may be driven by selective pressure enhancing the partitioning of the chemotypes, and not solely neutral demographic processes.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed pattern of haplotype and chemotype distribution.

claim: MAM1 and MAM2 are likely derived via a tandem duplication with ensuing divergence since the separation from A. lyrata
source: Supporting this potential is the observation that MAM1 and MAM2 are likely derived via a tandem duplication with ensuing divergence since the separation from A. lyrata (Figure 5—figure supplement 3; Benderoth et al., 2009; Benderoth et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by phylogenetic analysis and prior research.

claim: Alkenyl expressing accessions like Cvi-0 with an expressed copy of the AOP2 enzyme formed a single continuous cluster in the phylogenetic tree
source: Alkenyl expressing accessions like Cvi-0 with an expressed copy of the AOP2 enzyme formed a single continuous cluster (Figure 6A and Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a result from phylogenetic analysis of AOP sequences.

claim: Hydroxyalkyl (AOP3 expressed) accessions clustered into two separate groups
source: In contrast, hydroxyalkyl (AOP3 expressed) accessions clustered into two separate groups with one group of 3OHP-dominant accessions partitioning from the rest of the accessions at the most basal split in the tree (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A, AOP2 tree).
evidence: This is a result from phylogenetic analysis of AOP sequences.

claim: One hydroxyalkyl haplotype is marked by having an inversion swapping the AOP2 and AOP3 promoters as shown in bacterial artificial chromosome sequencing of the Ler-0 accession
source: This haplotype is marked by having an inversion swapping the AOP2 and AOP3 promoters as shown in bacterial artificial chromosome sequencing of the Ler-0 accession (Figure 6D; Chan et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by prior sequencing data.

claim: A small group of 3OHP accessions has a complete deletion of AOP2 and contains only AOP3
source: Analyzing the sequences of these accessions reveals that this small group of 3OHP accessions has a complete deletion of AOP2 and contains only AOP3 (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is a result from sequence analysis.

claim: There are at least two independent transitions from alkenyl to hydroxyalkyl glucosinolates within Arabidopsis
source: Thus, there are at least two independent transitions from alkenyl to hydroxyalkyl GSLs within Arabidopsis, neither of which are related to the alkenyl to hydroxyalkyl conversion within A. lyrata.
evidence: This is an inference from phylogenetic and sequence analysis.

claim: There are multiple alkenyl to hydroxyalkyl glucosinolate conversions both within and between Arabidopsis species
source: This indicates that there are multiple alkenyl to hydroxyalkyl GSL conversions both within and between Arabidopsis species.
evidence: This is an inference from phylogenetic and sequence analysis.

claim: Most of the null accessions harbor a 5 bps deletion in their AOP2 sequence, which causes a frameshift mutation
source: Most of the null accessions harbor a 5 bps deletion in their AOP2 sequence, which causes a frameshift mutation.
evidence: This is a result from sequence analysis.

claim: The 5 bp deletion mutation arose within the alkenyl haplotype and was first reported in the Col-0 reference genome
source: This mutation arose within the alkenyl haplotype and was first reported in the Col-0 reference genome (Figure 6B; Kliebenstein et al., 2001c).
evidence: This is supported by prior research and sequence analysis.

claim: There are additional independent loss-of-function events arising in both the alkenyl haplotype and within the Ler-0 inversion haplotype
source: In addition, there are additional independent LOF events arising in both the alkenyl haplotype (e.g., Sp-0, Figure 6C) and within the Ler-0 inversion haplotype (e.g., Fr-2, Figure 6F).
evidence: This is a result from sequence analysis.

claim: GS-AOP has repeated loss-of-function alleles arising within several of the major AOP haplotypes, suggesting convergent evolution of the MSO chemotype
source: Thus, GS-AOP has repeated LOF alleles arising within several of the major AOP haplotypes, suggesting convergent evolution of the MSO chemotype out of both the alkenyl and hydroxyalkyl chemotypes.
evidence: This is an inference from the pattern of loss-of-function mutations.

claim: The alkenyl haplotype is spread across the entire continent
source: The alkenyl haplotype is spread across the entire continent.
evidence: This is a finding from geographic analysis of haplotype distribution.

claim: The Ler-like 3OHP haplotype is present in only Central and North Europe
source: The Ler-like 3OHP haplotype is present in only Central and North Europe (Figure 6D)
evidence: This is a finding from geographic analysis of haplotype distribution.

claim: The 3OHP haplotype possessing only AOP3 is limited to Azerbaijan, along the Caspian Sea
source: while the other 3OHP haplotype, possessing only AOP3, is limited to Azerbaijan, along the Caspian Sea (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is a finding from geographic analysis of haplotype distribution.

claim: The independently derived loss-of-function null haplotypes are all located within Central and North Europe
source: In contrast to the distinct hydroxyalkyl locations, the distribution of the independent LOF null haplotypes overlaps with all of them being located within Central and North Europe (Figure 6B, C and F).
evidence: This is a finding from geographic analysis of haplotype distribution.

claim: The fact that independently derived loss-of-function alleles are all contiguous suggests that they may be beneficial or neutral in Central Europe
source: The fact that these independently derived LOF alleles are all contiguous suggests that they may be beneficial or neutral in Central Europe.
evidence: This is an inference from the geographic pattern of loss-of-function alleles.

claim: Previous work had suggested two GS-OH alleles measurable in the seed, a functional allele in almost all accessions and a non-functional allele caused by active site mutations represented by the Cvi-0 accession
source: Previous work had suggested two GS-OH alleles measurable in the seed, a functional allele in almost all accessions and a non-functional allele caused by active site mutations represented by the Cvi-0 accession (Hansen et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: 11 accessions were identified with a non-functional GS-OH
source: This identified 11 accessions with a non-functional GS-OH.
evidence: This is a result from phenotypic and sequence analysis.

claim: Multiple independent loss-of-function events were identified in GS-OH
source: Surveying these 11 accessions in the polymorph database (The 1001 Genomes Consortium, 2016) identified multiple independent LOF events.
evidence: This is a result from sequence analysis.

claim: One of the 11 non-functional GS-OH accessions has the Cvi active site mutations
source: One of these 11 accessions has the Cvi active site mutations, two accessions have a shared nonsense SNP that introduces premature stop codons and two accessions have a complete loss of this gene (Table 2).
evidence: This is a result from sequence analysis.

claim: Two accessions have a shared nonsense SNP that introduces premature stop codons in GS-OH
source: One of these 11 accessions has the Cvi active site mutations, two accessions have a shared nonsense SNP that introduces premature stop codons and two accessions have a complete loss of this gene (Table 2).
evidence: This is a result from sequence analysis.

claim: Two accessions have a complete loss of the GS-OH gene
source: One of these 11 accessions has the Cvi active site mutations, two accessions have a shared nonsense SNP that introduces premature stop codons and two accessions have a complete loss of this gene (Table 2).
evidence: This is a result from sequence analysis.

claim: All independent GS-OH loss-of-function alleles are found in accessions that do not accumulate 3-Butenyl glucosinolate
source: All these independent GS-OH LOF alleles are found in accessions that do not accumulate 3-Butenyl GSL, for example, three carbon or non-alkenyl accessions, suggesting that functional epistasis may be influencing the maintenance of these alleles in nature.
evidence: This is a finding from combined genotype and phenotype analysis.

claim: In all cases, the GS-OH loss-of-function allele is more frequent in the non four carbon-alkenyl accessions than expected by random chance
source: In all cases, the LOF allele is more frequent in the non four carbon-alkenyl accessions than expected by random chance.
evidence: This is a statistical finding from frequency analysis.

claim: There is selection against 3-Butenyl glucosinolate synthesis since loss-of-function alleles are more frequent when the GS-OH gene is cryptic by functional epistasis
source: This suggests that there is selection against 3-Butenyl GSL synthesis since LOF alleles are more frequent when the GS-OH gene is cryptic by functional epistasis.
evidence: This is an inference from the pattern of loss-of-function allele frequencies.

claim: The 3-Butenyl chemotype is the most sensitive to generalist lepidopteran herbivory
source: This agrees with the fact that the 3-Butenyl chemotype is the most sensitive to generalist lepidopteran herbivory (Hansen et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: GS-OH loss-of-function mutations may represent ongoing pseudogenization of the GS-OH gene when it is functionally hidden by epistasis at the GS-AOP and GS-Elong loci
source: Thus, these mutations may represent ongoing pseudogenization of the GS-OH gene when it is functionally hidden by epistasis at the GS-AOP and GS-Elong loci.
evidence: This is an inference from the pattern of loss-of-function mutations and epistasis.

claim: Environmental conditions, together with geography, affect the presence and distribution of chemotypes within the accessions
source: We found that environmental conditions, together with geography, affect the presence and distribution of chemotypes within the accessions.
evidence: This is a summary finding from the study's analyses.

claim: Chemotypic variation across Europe is created by a blend of genetics, geography, environment and demography that differ at the individual loci
source: This demonstrated that chemotypic variation across Europe is created by a blend of all these processes that differ at the individual loci.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion from the study's analyses.

claim: A simultaneous analysis of both genotype and phenotype is required to fully interpret the processes shaping metabolic variation
source: This implies that a simultaneous analysis of both genotype and phenotype is required to fully interpret these processes and relationships.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the study's findings.

claim: Glucosinolates have mainly been linked to influencing biotic interaction with herbivores considered the primary drivers shaping glucosinolate genetic diversity
source: GSLs have been mainly linked to influencing biotic interaction with herbivores considered the primary drivers shaping GSL genetic diversity.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge in the field.

claim: Climate drives the distribution of biotic factors like herbivores, so climatic factors might appear as indirectly associated with glucosinolates
source: However, because climate drives the distribution of biotic factors like herbivores, it is likely that climatic factors might appear as indirectly associated with GSLs.
evidence: This is an inference about the relationship between climate and biotic factors.

claim: An aliphatic glucosinolate was recently mechanistically linked to drought resistance in Arabidopsis
source: Interestingly, an aliphatic GSL was recently mechanistically linked to drought resistance in Arabidopsis, suggesting a potential role for abiotic factors to influence GSL diversity (Salehin et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to recent research.

claim: All three major aliphatic glucosinolate loci display extensive allelic heterogeneity that is shaped by a blend of evolutionary events at each locus reminiscent of either parallel or convergent evolution
source: All three major aliphatic GSL loci display extensive allelic heterogeneity that is shaped by a blend of evolutionary events at each locus reminiscent of either parallel or convergent evolution.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion from the genetic analyses.

claim: GS-OH provided clear evidence of parallel evolution where a single functional haplotype gave rise to at least four independent loss-of-function alleles
source: GS-OH provided clear evidence of parallel evolution where a single functional haplotype gave rise to at least four independent LOF alleles all with similar phenotypic consequence.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the genetic analysis of GS-OH.

claim: GS-AOP suggested the potential for convergent evolution-style events leading to MSO chemotype arising from loss-of-function events at the GS-AOP locus
source: GS-AOP suggested the potential for convergent evolution-style events leading to MSO chemotype arising from LOF events at the GS-AOP locus.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the genetic analysis of GS-AOP.

claim: The same glucosinolate chemotype, MSO, arises from independent loss-of-function alleles in two different genes, AOP2 and AOP3, that represent two different ancestral haplotypes
source: Thus, the same GSL chemotype, MSO, arises from independent LOF alleles in two different genes, AOP2 and AOP3, that represent two different ancestral haplotypes (Figure 6).
evidence: This is a finding from genetic analysis showing convergent evolution.

claim: Parallel-style events occur at all the major glucosinolate loci
source: Thus, it appears that parallel-style events occur at all the loci and at least at the GS-AOP locus there is potential for a convergent-style evolutionary event leading to a single chemotype.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion from the genetic analyses.

claim: Three-way epistasis is shaping the allelic heterogeneity at these loci and their evolutionary potential
source: In addition to independent evolutionary events, three-way epistasis is shaping the allelic heterogeneity at these loci and their evolutionary potential.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the analysis of genetic interactions.

claim: The multiple independent GS-OH loss-of-function variants all appear to have arisen in lineages where the GS-AOP and GS-Elong loci had haplotypes that epistatically combined to block the formation of the but-3-enyl glucosinolate precursor for GS-OH
source: For example, the multiple independent GS-OH LOF variants all appear to have arisen in lineages where the GS-AOP and GS-Elong loci had haplotypes that epistatically combined to block the formation of the but-3-enyl GSL precursor for GS-OH (Figure 2).
evidence: This is a finding from combined genetic and phenotypic analysis.

claim: The parallel evolution of GS-OH loss-of-function alleles is epistatically conditioned by GS-AOP and GS-Elong
source: Thus, the parallel evolution of GS-OH LOF alleles is epistatically conditioned by GS-AOP and GS-Elong.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the analysis of epistatic interactions.

claim: Both AOP3 alleles of GS-AOP are coordinated with C3 haplotypes in GS-Elong
source: Both of AOP3 alleles of GS-AOP are coordinated with C3 haplotypes in GS-Elong.
evidence: This is a finding from combined genetic analysis.

claim: A functional MAM1 leads to the creation of C4 glucosinolates regardless of the functional state of the MAM2 gene
source: There is also within-locus epistasis in the GS-Elong locus wherein a functional MAM1 leads to the creation of C4 GSLs regardless of the functional state of the MAM2 gene
evidence: This is a statement of epistatic relationships based on genetic knowledge.

claim: C3 haplotypes are marked by the loss of MAM1
source: and C3 haplotypes are marked by the loss of MAM1.
evidence: This is a finding from genetic analysis.

claim: The clade 4 haplotype of GS-Elong can equally mutate to create a C3 or C4 chemotype because it has both MAM1 and MAM2
source: For example, the clade 4 haplotype of GS-Elong can equally mutate to create a C3 or C4 chemotype because it has both MAM1 and MAM2.
evidence: This is an inference about evolutionary potential based on genetic structure.

claim: The loss of MAM1 likely prevents the ability for C3 lineages to recreate the C4 chemotype
source: In this case, the loss of MAM1 likely prevents the ability for this C3 lineage to recreate the C4 chemotype.
evidence: This is an inference about evolutionary constraints based on genetic structure.

claim: The potential evolutionary trajectory of a haplotype/allele at one or within one of these glucosinolate loci may be epistatically conditioned by the allelic state all the loci within a specific lineage
source: Thus, the potential evolutionary trajectory of a haplotype/allele at one or even within one of these GSL loci may be epistatically conditioned by the allelic state all the loci within a specific lineage.
evidence: This is a conclusion about evolutionary constraints from epistatic analysis.

claim: Brassica ssp. have genetic variation at GS-Elong and GS-AOP creating the exact same chemotypic variation found in Arabidopsis
source: Confounding this further is the observation that Brassica ssp. have genetic variation at GS-Elong and GS-AOP creating the exact same chemotypic variation found in Arabidopsis (Heidel et al., 2006; Ramos-Onsins et al., 2004; Windsor et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: There is similar within-species (GS-AOP) and between-species (GS-AOP and GS-Elong) variation between the closely related Arabidopsis sister species, A. lyrata, A. petraea and A. halleri
source: There is similar within-species (GS-AOP) and between-species (GS-AOP and GS-Elong) variation between the closely related Arabidopsis sister species, A. lyrata, A. petraea and A. halleri.
evidence: This is a statement about variation patterns across related species.

claim: The underlying genetic basis of glucosinolate variation is independent events at the AOP and MAM loci showing that the variation did not go through the speciation boundary
source: However, the underlying genetic basis is independent events at the AOP and MAM loci showing that the variation did not go through the speciation boundary.
evidence: This is an inference about evolutionary history from genetic analysis.

claim: Glucosinolate variation has been recreated repeatedly in Arabidopsis species
source: Instead, this suggests that this variation has been recreated repeatedly in these species
evidence: This is an inference about evolutionary patterns from genetic analysis.

claim: Previous work on pathogen resistance gene-for-gene loci indicated a predominant model of having two moderate-frequency ancient alleles creating the phenotypic variation within the species
source: Previous work on other biotic interactions genes like pathogen resistance gene-for-gene loci had indicated a predominant model of having two moderate-frequency ancient alleles creating the phenotypic variation within the species (Atwell et al., 2010; Corrion and Day, 2001; MacQueen et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The glucosinolate loci are characterized by a blend of structural and SNP-based variation with numerous alleles that appear young
source: In contrast to R-gene loci characterized by old/stable biallelic variation, the GSL loci are characterized by a blend of structural and SNP-based variation with numerous alleles that appear young.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion from the genetic analyses.

claim: Natural variation in the immune gene ACCELERATED CELL DEATH 6 (ACD6) is caused by a rare allele causing an extreme lesion phenotype
source: In other cases, alleles of genes involved in biotic defense can present more complex patterns, for example, natural variation in the immune gene ACCELERATED CELL DEATH 6 (ACD6) is caused by a rare allele causing an extreme lesion phenotype.
evidence: This is a statement about variation in another defense gene.

claim: It is not yet clear what selective pressures influence ACD6 genetic variation
source: It is not yet clear what selective pressures influence ACD6 genetic variation (Todesco et al., 2010; Zhu et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Loci controlling resistance to diverse biotic traits under natural conditions have diverse genetic architectures
source: Thus, loci controlling resistance to diverse biotic traits under natural conditions have diverse genetic architectures and further work is needed to assess the range of allelic heterogeneity in these adaptive loci.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from comparing different defense loci.

claim: The Iberian Peninsula and the Mediterranean Basin had low variability in aliphatic glucosinolate chemotypes, which show strong geographic structure
source: For example, the Iberian Peninsula and the Mediterranean Basin had low variability in aliphatic GSL chemotypes, which show strong geographic structure.
evidence: This is a finding from geographic analysis of chemotype distribution.

claim: Central/North Europe had high aliphatic glucosinolate diversity with chemotypes showing overlapping geographic distributions
source: By contrast, Central/North Europe had high aliphatic GSL diversity with chemotypes showing overlapping geographic distributions.
evidence: This is a finding from geographic analysis of chemotype distribution.

claim: The Iberian Peninsula and the Mediterranean Basin are genetically diverse
source: At first glance, this contrasts with previous work showing that the Iberian Peninsula and the Mediterranean Basin are genetically diverse.
evidence: This is a statement about prior findings on genetic diversity.

claim: The GS-AOP locus was largely fixed as the Alkenyl allele in Iberia/Mediterranean Basin with the alternative GS-AOP alleles enriched in Central Europe
source: Specifically, the GS-AOP locus was largely fixed as the Alkenyl allele in Iberia/Mediterranean Basin with the alternative GS-AOP alleles enriched in Central Europe.
evidence: This is a finding from geographic analysis of allele distribution.

claim: Iberia and the Mediterranean Basin were highly genetically diverse for the GS-Elong locus and appear to contain almost all the variation in GS-Elong found throughout Europe
source: In contrast to GS-AOP, Iberia and the Mediterranean Basin were highly genetically diverse for the GS-Elong locus and appear to contain almost all the variation in GS-Elong found throughout Europe (The 1001 Genomes Consortium, 2016).
evidence: This is a finding from geographic analysis of allele distribution.

claim: The chemotypic divergence from genomic variation expectations was driven by just the GS-AOP locus
source: Thus, the chemotypic divergence from genomic variation expectations was driven by just the GS-AOP locus.
evidence: This is a conclusion from comparing chemotype and genotype patterns.

claim: The high level of chemotypic variation in Central Europe is a blend of alleles that emerged in the south (GS-Elong) and alleles that possibly arose locally (GS-AOP, both nulls and AOP3)
source: This indicates that the high level of chemotypic variation in Central Europe is a blend of alleles that emerged in the south (GS-Elong) and alleles that possibly arose locally (GS-AOP, both nulls and AOP3).
evidence: This is an inference about the origin of alleles from geographic patterns.

claim: The chemotypes found in any one region appear to be created by a combination of alleles as a result of a gene flow across the continent, local generation of new polymorphisms and local selective pressures
source: Further, the chemotypes found in any one region appear to be created by a combination of alleles as a result of a gene flow across the continent, local generation of new polymorphisms and local selective pressures.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion about the processes shaping chemotype distribution.

claim: The genome-wide association with this collection of 797 accessions was unable to find 80% of the known causal loci
source: Specifically, the GWA with this collection of 797 accessions was unable to find 80% of the known causal loci including one of the three major effect loci, GS-OH.
evidence: This is a finding about the limitations of genome-wide association in this study.

claim: Maximizing the number of genotypes and the SNP marker density was unable to overcome the complications imposed by the complex pressures shaping the distribution of these traits
source: Maximizing the number of genotypes and the SNP marker density was unable to overcome the complications imposed by the complex pressures shaping the distribution of these traits, potentially due to unequal dense sampling from the different areas.
evidence: This is a conclusion about the limitations of genome-wide association.

claim: In complex adaptive systems, the optimal solution to identifying causal variants is likely a blend of structured mapping populations and then translating the causal genes from this system to the genome-wide association results
source: In complex adaptive systems, the optimal solution to identifying causal variants is likely a blend of structured mapping populations and then translating the causal genes from this system to the GWA results and tracking the causal loci directly.
evidence: This is a recommendation based on the study's findings.

claim: Seeds for 1135 Arabidopsis genotypes were obtained from the 1001 genomes catalog
source: Seeds for 1135 Arabidopsis (A. thaliana) genotypes were obtained from the 1001 genomes catalog of A. thaliana genetic variation (https://1001genomes.org/).
evidence: This is a description of the plant material used in the study.

claim: All Arabidopsis genotypes were grown at 22°C/24°C (day/night) under long-day conditions (16 hr of light/8 hr of dark)
source: All Arabidopsis genotypes were grown at 22°C/24°C (day/night) under long-day conditions (16 hr of light/8 hr of dark).
evidence: This is a description of the growth conditions used in the study.

claim: Two independent replicates were performed, each of them included the full set of genotypes
source: Two independent replicates were performed, each of them included the full set of genotypes.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental design.

claim: Only accessions from Europe and around Europe were included in the analyses, resulting in an analysis of 797 accessions
source: In the analyses, only accessions from Europe and around Europe were included (Figure 3A), resulting in an analysis of 797 accessions.
evidence: This is a description of the data filtering for analysis.

claim: Glucosinolates were measured from approximately 3 mg of seeds
source: Briefly, ~3 mg of seeds were harvested in 200 μL of 90% methanol.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental method.

claim: Individual desulfo-glucosinolates within each sample were separated and detected by HPLC-DAD
source: Individual desulfo-GSLs within each sample were separated and detected by HPLC-DAD, identified, quantified by comparison to standard curves from purified compounds and further normalized to the weight.
evidence: This is a description of the analytical method.

claim: Broad-sense heritability for the different metabolites was estimated by taking the variance due to accession and dividing it by the total variance
source: Broad-sense heritability (Supplementary file 1C) for the different metabolites was estimated from this model by taking the variance due to accession and dividing it by the total variance.
evidence: This is a description of the statistical method.

claim: Genome-wide association was implemented with the easyGWAS tool using the EMMAX algorithms and a minor allele frequency cutoff of 5%
source: GWA was implemented with the easyGWAS tool (Grimm et al., 2017) using the EMMAX algorithms (Kang et al., 2010) and a minor allele frequency (MAF) cutoff of 5%.
evidence: This is a description of the genome-wide association method.

claim: Multiple sequence alignment was done with the msa package in R using the ClustalW, ClustalOmega and Muscle algorithms
source: Multiple sequence alignment was done with the msa package (default settings) in R using the ClustalW, ClustalOmega and Muscle algorithms (Bodenhofer et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a description of the phylogenetic analysis method.

claim: Phylogenetic trees were generated with the 'ape' package (neighbor-joining tree)
source: Phylogenetic trees were generated with the 'ape' package (neighbor-joining tree) (Paradis and Schliep, 2019) and were visualized with ggtree package in R (Yu, 2020).
evidence: This is a description of the phylogenetic analysis method.

claim: PacBio long read-based de novo genome assemblies of the relevant accession were generated as part of the 1001 Genomes Plus project
source: PacBio long read-based de novo genome assemblies of the relevant accession were generated as part of the 1001 Genomes Plus project.
evidence: This is a description of the sequencing method.

claim: The genomes were assembled with Canu (v1.71) and polished using the long reads followed by a second polishing step with PCR-free short reads
source: The genomes were assembled with Canu (v1.71) (Koren et al., 2017) and polished using the long reads followed by a second polishing step with PCR-free short reads.
evidence: This is a description of the genome assembly method.
